title: The Tune on the Heap
style: Folk-club: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, low cello drone, brushed snare, a warm male baritone with a little gravel — the sound of a busker's last note hanging in cold air, half-remembered.
lyrics:

[chorus]

[verse]

[chorus]
So I'll keep the sound in a little brass ball,

title: The Tune on the Heap
style: Sparse acoustic folk ballad, fingerpicked nylon guitar, soft brushed snare, one warm male voice, a low cello line. Quiet, intimate, a little melancholy, the sound of a room after the lights go out.
lyrics:
[verse]
The fuse went down at half past four,
and the kitchen went to black and blue.
I set the kettle where I couldn't see
and I sat there thinking what I'd make if I could make anything,
and the dark held its breath
and it held it all night long.

[chorus]
So I'll catch the tune before it goes,
the busker's coin on the heap,
one you'd never heard before,
gone before you could ask
what it was,
what it was.

[verse]
I've rubbed the handle, rubbed the plate,
I've built the row of chairs to sit.
But this is the one I didn't plan,
a sound with no name,
a sound with no hands.

[chorus]
So I'll catch the tune before it goes,
the busker's coin on the heap,
one you'd never heard before,
gone before you could ask
what it was,
what it was.

[outro]
And the lamp still glows
where the dark let go,
and the heap keeps its things —
the coin, the note,
the sound,
the sound.

Every window has a candle bright
And I'm counting down the miles tonight

[chorus]
I'll be home by Christmas Eve
Save a place by the fire for me
Through the snow and the winter freeze
I'll be home by Christmas Eve

[verse]
Kids are hanging stockings on the stair
Grandad snoring in his favourite chair
Somebody's singing out of tune again
And I wouldn't change it, not one thing

[chorus]
I'll be home by Christmas Eve
Save a place by the fire for me
Through the snow and the winter freeze
I'll be home by Christmas Eve

[bridge]
Ring the bells, ring the bells
Let the whole world sing
Ring the bells, ring the bells
For the joy it brings

[chorus]
I'll be home by Christmas Eve
Save a place by the fire for me
Through the snow and the winter freeze
I'll be home by Christmas Eve

[chorus]
I'll be home by Christmas Eve
Save a place by the fire for me
Through the snow and the winter freeze
I'll be home by Christmas Eve

[outro]
I'll be home
By Christmas Eve

title: Fair Wage, Big Plate
style: brass band march, 118bpm, B-flat major, bright cornets and tuba, driving march beat, singalong chorus in a warm male voice, a bit of street-corner grit
lyrics:
[verse]
Up the hill on a maroon banner
Votes and bread for every lass
We stand on boxes in the morning
Not on crumbs and not on glass

[chorus]
Fair wage, big plate
Fair wage, big plate
Nobody works for a single pea
Fair wage, big plate
Fair wage, big plate
Stand on a box and you'll be seen

title: Tarantella of Lesina
style: Apulian tarantella, fast 160bpm, staccato guitar-like plucks, pizzicato strings, clapping, lively male vocal singing in Italian, major key, danceable and brash
lyrics:
[verse]
Sotto il mare che non è mare
acqua salata, sole che brilla
dove va la barca alla sera
torna sempre a casa, non va via
[chorus]
Tarantella, tarantella
batti i piedi, batti forte
dove va la gente alla sera
venga a mangiar con il mio cordon
